message.content:
Here are some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller movies released in 2020 (in no particular order):

| Title | Director(s) | Notable Cast | Why it stood out |
|-------|-------------|--------------|------------------|
| **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A fresh take on the classic horror‑thriller formula, blending psychological suspense with sci‑fi twists. |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | Nolan’s mind‑bending time‑travel thriller that kept audiences guessing about cause and effect. |
| **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced, witty crime caper featuring a star‑packed ensemble. |
| **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Whitehead | A chilling psychological thriller that uses a haunted house as a metaphor for grief and trauma. |
| **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A tense, claustrophobic thriller about a group of strangers trapped in a remote cabin. |
| **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A historical crime‑drama that blends medieval intrigue with modern storytelling techniques. |
| **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Anya Taylor‑Joy, Riley Keough | A bleak, atmospheric crime‑drama that explores violence and morality in rural America. |
| **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic crime saga that uses de‑scanning technology to tell a long‑form story about aging mobsters. |
| **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu‑Urri | Zorion Eguileor, Iván Massagué | A dystopian thriller that critiques social inequality through a brutal, claustrophobic setting. |
| **The Lodge** | Severin Fiala & Veronika Franz | Riley Keough, Toni Collette | A psychological thriller that blurs the line between supernatural horror and human manipulation. |

These films were praised for their direction, performances, and ability to keep viewers on edge. If you’re looking for something specific—like a sub‑genre, a particular director, or a certain tone—just let me know!
